question_text: Given that at 20 °C a Cu–0.1 wt% Si alloy has a resistivity of ρ₍₂₀ °C₎=23.6×10⁻⁹ Ω·m, and that the temperature coefficient of resistivity of copper (and its dilute alloys) is α=0.00393 °C⁻¹, estimate the resistivity of the Cu–0.1 wt% Si alloy at 100 °C.The unit of the answer is \Omega \cdot \mathrm{m}.
response:
Using the linear temperature dependence of resistivity:

$$\rho(T) = \rho(T_0)\,[1 + \alpha\,(T - T_0)]$$

with $T - T_0 = 100 - 20 = 80\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$:

$$\rho(100^\circ\mathrm{C}) = 23.6\times10^{-9}\,[1 + 0.00393 \times 80] = 23.6\times10^{-9}\times 1.3144 \approx 3.10\times10^{-8}\ \Omega\cdot\mathrm{m}$$

$$\boxed{3.10\times10^{-8}}$$
